body.text: The inventory's `proof` field reads `stale` (20), `missing` (7) or `exercised_unrecorded` (1): it records proof-run freshness on 2026-11-05, not whether a test exists.

Three inventory rows are `impl: absent` at the lock: `inv_prison_no_bed`, `inv_toss_flame`, `inv_raider_fetch_fallen`. Their leaves (`drained_hole_is_a_prison`, `toss_flame_from_rim`, `raiders_fetch_their_fallen`) are owed code, not owed tests. (`inv_irrigation`, `unknown` at the lock, left for 0.2.0.)

Every live scene's tier says "quicktest", but the `tier_reason` of 25 of 31 leaves is one boiler-plate sentence ("an on-screen look and a live state change: needs a running map"). Whether a faster test decides each is the Stage 4 challenger's question; the reason is written, not shown true.

The C# SelfTest is one console app holding most of the offline checks (325+ cases); a Python wrapper `src/RimMandrake/Utils/selftest_flowworks_stock.py` builds it with Windows `dotnet.exe`. One run covers many bars.

The Stage 3 offline checks of five bars are source laws, not behaviour runs (`selftest_stage3_owed.py`): the code is Verse-bound. They decide "the code that would make the bar true exists and has this shape"; whether it works is the scene's question at Stage 6.

The 10-18 T6 FAIL (dehydration 0.075) was not a mod defect: it traced to the pre-025f7fdbfa harness, which did not draft the pawn, so the pawn drank.

body.text: Shuttle plant now keeps one pair and moves 1 dL, tripping no other law; the 24-pulse window runs per-pulse checks and counts no filling body. settling/kernel_fuzz PROVEN red 13/10000 by settled_scene_reaches_fixed_point, baseline 0/10000.

The original shuttle was assumed to reverse or continue: it need not, since with depths [2,2] and water [U,U] the first move leaves [2U,0] and neither cell is eligible again; the pair is not kept between calls and need not be adjacent (Codex finding 3).

Settling proves on 10000 scenes because only 58/10000 are settled-expected; a smaller run may not reach the law. Codex's remaining per-fluid/sink/count findings stay open in RIMMANDRAKE_FIX_FLOWWORKS_FUZZ_FOUR_FLAWS_SINK_STILL_FLOAT.

The FlowWorks conservation law (volume_in_equals_out_plus_stored, FlowKernelFuzz.cs) did not see 1 dL appearing from nowhere: its float tolerance of 1e-3 levels equals 10 dL (U = 10000 dL/level), so a sub-level leak passed (0/300 red over 1156 plants).
body.proposed_fix: Make the law exact in decilitres and have ShippedMatrixProbe plant one dL (k.water[i] += 1).
body.accept: vv_laws.py prove FlowWorks --family conservation with the 1 dL plant is PROVEN; NOT_PROVEN on the base.

body.text: The law now compares exactly in dL instead of the 10 dL float tolerance, and the probe plants one dL. Prove on base NOT_PROVEN (0/300, planted 1156); after PROVEN (baseline 0/300, red 162/300); unplanted 10000 scenes 0 failures.
The kernel re-rounding a cell to whole levels each pulse (which would make the law right) was ruled out: the kernel does not round the decilitre away; the check was wrong, not the mod.
The law's tolerance was in levels (1e-3 level = 10 dL), so a green kernel_fuzz did not mean sub-level volume was conserved; a whole level went red 141/300 but one dL went 0/300.
